page: Microsoft Azure D16s_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor with 16 vCPUs, 8 physical cores, and 2 threads per core. The processor operates at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz and includes a 260 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2134.0 and single-threaded gzip compression reaching 31.24 GB/sec. Text processing capabilities are also strong, scoring 2718.0 in Geekbench. Multi-core performance is average, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 15986.8 and a Passmark CPU score of 26651.67. Memory bandwidth tests show 1239.67 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 124.24 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. The processor supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and int8 operations, which assist in workload acceleration.

This server configuration does not include local storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, meaning storage requirements must be met using external Premium Storage options. The lack of bundled local storage and GPUs represents a clear tradeoff, positioning this instance as a cost-efficient choice for workloads that do not require high-speed local scratch disks or hardware acceleration. It offers a balanced resource density of compute and memory for standard enterprise applications.

The D16s_v6 is suited for general-purpose enterprise workloads, including static web serving, database operations, software compilation, and moderate-scale text or image processing. It is also capable of handling small to medium language model inference, achieving 332.76 tokens/sec for text generation on a 135M model and 15.78 tokens/sec on a 7B model.
